discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body systems with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller (with Jaksch and co-workers, 1998) showed theoretically that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model, with interactions and tunnelling that can be tuned from the outside. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator, the first time a textbook model of strongly correlated matter was built and controlled atom by atom. This started the field of analogue quantum simulation. Later work by these nominees includes quantum gas microscopes with single-site resolution (Greiner, Bloch), antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, many-body localization, and proposals for simulating lattice gauge theories. Together these results turned Feynman's idea of a quantum simulator into a working laboratory tool. They now probe questions in condensed matter, high-energy physics and quantum information that classical computers cannot answer, and they influence how a whole generation of physicists thinks about many-body quantum systems.
